text:
The stock jumped 2.3% today as oil prices surged on Middle East tensions—specifically reports that President Trump's administration is considering large-scale military operations in Iran, which would threaten a major global oil supply source. With U.S. crude at $96 and world oil at $125, refineries are running at 92.7% capacity, meaning Marathon Petroleum has strong margins to turn crude into fuel at a time when fuel prices are exceptionally high and tight.

The stock's 14% climb over two weeks reflects a broader shift: geopolitical risk in the Persian Gulf, combined with a global diesel shortage driving up both crude prices and the value of refined products, has made refining highly profitable right now. Shipping costs have also exploded (a single tanker charter from the Gulf just cost $76 million, ten times normal rates), which keeps prices elevated across the board and benefits refiners positioned to sell into this tight market.
